newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy may reduce number of debt auctions - sources.
newsitem.headline: Italy may reduce number of debt auctions - sources.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is studying a rationalisation plan which might lead to it reducing the total of monthly debt auctions, monetary and market sources said.
The Treasury currently holds 20 auctions a month, six for short-term bills (BOT), four for zero-coupon certificates (CTZ), eight for fixed-coupon bonds (BTP) and two for floating-rate notes (CCT).
The first change, possibly from April, could mean the Treasury offering BOTs only at an end-month auction, abolishing the mid-month sale, the sources said.
The Treasury is also studying the possible reopening of 12-month BOTs to given more volume to the paper, by reopening the 12-month BOT after six months and after nine months.
One monetary source said a reduction in the number of medium to long-term paper auctions was also being examined.

The reason for the possible changes in BOT sales stemmed from the increase in variation between mid and end-month rates, particularly on the three-month BOT, which has been noted for several months due to a more marked Treasury strategy of a reduction in its offer of short-term paper.
In the opening months of this year, the minimum variation in the gross yield of three-month BOTs between two consecutive autions was 64 basis points and a maximum of 86 bps.
"The unification of BOTs into the end-month auction would end this oscillation which does not mirror market rates," one specialist dealer said.
"The Treasury has its own good reasons in continuing to reduce the offer of short-term paper," he added.
Specialist government bond traders have in the past few days sent the Treasury their opinions on possible changes to the current auction system.
